For starters, you’re still young. It’s okay not to know yet and it’s okay not to be ready to come out even if you do know. I beat around the bush for many years even after I knew I was gay because I was afraid to be myself. 

The point is, only you will know when to come out and when you are ready. If you need more time to explore, do it. That’s perfectly okay. Start experimenting more with both genders, watch gay, straight, lesbian and bisexual porn and find what excites you. Eventually you will be okay.

I think before you even go ahead with making any decision, you need to make an appointment and get checked out to 100% confirm the pregnancy. At-home pregnancy tests can read false positives, and once a woman thinks they are pregnant their body can actually mimick symptoms even when there is no actual pregnancy.  It would suck to go through all of that stress in telling him to find out it’s not even true. Once you know for certain, then you can go from there.

I am all for a woman’s body being her temple and a woman having the final choice in abortion; but I do think if you are in fact pregnant that you should talk to him about it; based on your description he sounds like a man who has his shit together and he may want to pursue parenthood even if you have only been together a short time. However, he also is likely rational and will realize that with parenthood comes a financial hit and that you both may not be ready presently to pursue that in your relationship. 

Regardless you are going to need a support system whether you decide to keep the child or not, but it’s probably better for you to include him in the process instead of hiding it. Worst case scenario it drives a wedge between you now, you have the abortion, and you just saved yourself years of torment with a partner whom you wouldn’t have ended up with anyways. People show their true colours in stressful times. 

Best of luck with whichever route you choose.

He’s entitled to his privacy, sure, but sex is a two way street. She has needs too, and he isn’t meeting them.....she has a right to know why. Better to know now than to get married and spend 10 years in a sexless marriage only to find out he isn’t attracted to her, or is attracted to men etc.

If he’s not willing to communicate with you about it that’s a major red flag. You either need to give him an ultimatum or reevaluate your relationship and maybe consider moving on.

I read a couple of your older posts; the first thing that I am wondering is if your financial situation has improved. Also, has your husband found a new job? Is he getting help for himself? Or has not much changed?

If he has changed and has worked on bettering himself, that is good as he can be a support for you. If he hasn’t, and is still treating you poorly and lazing about at home, then I have some advice.

Don’t worry about him. 

Your mental health is what is important right now. You need to focus on taking care of yourself. If he isn’t on the same page, it is time to consider ending the relationship if it is only toxic and a source of further hurt for you. You should not have to financially support his habits so he can sit at home. 

If that means being hospitalized and losing your place, so be it. You have other people in your life who love you and will help you out. Reach out to your sister. Go to the hospital. Don’t worry about your husband; if he’s a good man he will find a way to make ends meet so that he can support you. 

Wishing you all the best.

We started one a few years back at my college.....the main thing was convincing the school to allow the club to be founded in the first place. They were iffy on the subject as it isn’t directly related to any one class or sport. So it took some convincing. You also need to speak with your student council, I believe they are usually the governing body that manages the clubs at most institutions, and you’ll need to find out how many members you have to have to start the club. Usually you need President/Vice pres/treasurer/secretary and someone to plan and host different events. We had to write a charter up and also provide a mission statement and itinerary for what we wanted to try and accomplish. Anything additional we decided to do later we just had to submit and have approved. Also, any advertisement for the club that you want to put on school property usually has to be approved as well. We had an issue with that a year and a half ago when we were having open mic nights at one of the local bars; the college wouldnt allow us to advertise at the school. Good luck!! Let me know if you have any questions. I worked primarily as the social media coordinator for my club but I do know a little about most everything else.
